title: Sub-Harmonic Injection Locking and Gyrotropic Parity Symmetry Breaking in a Low-Pressure Argon Standing-Wave RF Cavity Processor

creators.name: Grimm, Justin D.
creators.affiliation: Independent Dandelion Substrate Research Group, Gurley, Alabama 35748, USA

description: Complete theoretical derivation, benchtop link budget, parametric 21-port vacuum vessel CAD, 13-channel zero-IF homodyne receiver KiCad netlist generator, freestanding ISO C99 64-byte SPI DMA safety daemon, and synthesizable Lattice iCE40HX8K-CT256 Verilog RTL arbiter (v1.1.0) for a balanced-ternary standing-wave radio-frequency cavity processor. Operating on the spherical TM101 eigenmode at 915.0 MHz inside low-pressure Argon (1.067 kPa, Ramsauer-Townsend scattering minimum), a coherent third-harmonic pump at 2.745 GHz quantizes continuous modal phases into three symmetric 120-degree attractors {-1, 0, +1}. Weak-interaction beta helicity from an exempt 37.0 kBq Co-60 source paired with a sub-cyclotron 28.0 mT axial Helmholtz guide field induces off-diagonal plasma gyrotropy (10.50-degree non-reciprocal Sakaguchi phase lag), breaking dihedral D3 stagnation into unidirectional C3 chiral soliton relaxation, while modulo-13 decimated 37.0 kBq Am-241 ionization pulses provide a crystal-free 104.0 Hz Erlang-13 frame clock.
notes: Reproducibility verification: run `make verify` (seed 42, execution time < 5 s) to audit 21-port mechanical clearances, generate fixed-point Q2.14 CAD phase-trim lookup tables, verify 42-pin FPGA BGA ball parity, execute 7 freestanding C11 safety-interlock unit tests across 64-byte SPI DMA and 65,536-byte ring structures, and run the self-checking IEEE 1364-2005 Verilog testbench.
